newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arabs proposing freezing ties with Israel - paper.
newsitem.headline: Arabs proposing freezing ties with Israel - paper.

text.p: An Egyptian government newspaper said on Thursday that Egypt, Saudi Arabia and the Palestinians are proposing Arab and Islamic countries freeze ties with Israel immediately and withdraw from any joint economic projects.

The newspaper al-Akhbar said that in a joint proposal to a meeting of the Jerusalem Committee in Morocco on Thursday they also suggest setting up a fund of at least $1 billion to protect Islamic sites in Jerusalem and buy land there from Jews.
Egyptian foreign ministry officials were not immediately available to comment on the unsourced report.

The proposal is a response to the Israeli government's decision to build a Jewish housing or settlement project in Arab East Jerusalem -- an act which Arab states say violates peace agreements between Israel and the Palestinians.

Al-Akhbar said: "Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Palestine have presented a draft, to be discussed by the Jerusalem Committee, including measures to save Jerusalem, oblige Arab and Islamic states to freeze relations with Israel immediately, withdraw from any economic and commercial projects to which Israel is a partner and to suspend multilateral negotiations."

"(It also includes) quickly setting up a fund with a capital of at least $1 billion, earmarked to protect the Islamic holy places in Jerusalem, to buy land from Jews and to support the Arab residents of the city so that they do not give up their land and property under Zionist enticements," it added.

Israel's groundbreaking on the settlement in East Jerusalem, occupied by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war, has also enraged Palestinians who regard East Jerusalem as the capital of a future independent Palestinian state.

Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa, speaking in Syria on Wednesday before leaving for Morocco for the meeting, said the Jerusalem Committee would take a position based on the resolutions of the Islamic summit in Islamabad last weekend.

The summit urged Islamic states to "review relations with Israel and make them contingent on the progress achieved in the peace process, and on the extent to which Israel complies with U.N. resolutions and with agreements, commitments and obligations reached by the parties concerned".
But an Egyptian official said this week that countries which have peace treaties with Israel are exempt from the appeal.
Under the Israeli-Egyptian peace treaty of 1979, Egypt had an obligation to set up normal relations with the Jewish state.
